note: New Zealand's four largest banks are ANZ, ASB, BNZ and Westpac. ASB's and Westpac's card rates-and-fees pages answer 403, and ANZ's pages carry Incapsula and now load their rates by script, which this research doesn't render (2026-10-30); so ANZ's Low Rate Visa is kept as read on 2026-10-29 and BNZ's two cards on sale are added. ANZ New Zealand's page for its Low Rate Visa (read 2026-10-29): no annual card fee, and 13.90% a year on purchases (kept as read). BNZ's pages (read 2026-10-30): the Lite Visa, 13.50% a year on purchases and 22.95% on cash advances, a 5-dollar half-yearly account fee, up to 55 days interest-free, and a minimum monthly repayment of 2% of the balance or 25 dollars, whichever is more; the Advantage Visa Platinum, 18.95% a year on purchases and cash advances, a 45-dollar half-yearly account fee, up to 44 interest-free days (its minimum repayment isn't stated on its page and isn't written); for both, a cash advance in New Zealand 0.90 dollars (none on overseas withdrawals), a late payment fee of 2 dollars, and a foreign currency service fee of 2.25% of the NZ dollar value. BNZ's cards no longer on sale (Advantage Visa Classic, the Private Bank Advantage Visa Platinum) and its business cards aren't written. Wave 4 (2026-10-30): Q Card's Q Mastercard, one of the country's widely held non-bank credit cards, is added as a third issuer, its fees page being open; Kiwibank's and Westpac's sites didn't answer, ASB's, TSB's and the Co-operative Bank's answer 403 or Incapsula's block, Gem (Latitude) carries Incapsula and Heartland a captcha (2026-10-30). Q Card's fees and charges page (read 2026-10-30), the Q Mastercard: a standard interest rate of 28.95% a year and 29.50% on cash advances; an account fee of 50 dollars a year charged as 25 dollars on opening and every six months, written as a half-yearly fee; a domestic cash advance 2 dollars at an ATM (3 at a teller, and 3 or 6.50 abroad, not written); the international transaction fee 1.4%; a default fee of 15 dollars when a payment isn't received in full by the due date. The long-term-finance establishment and advance fees and the paper statement fee aren't written; the Q Card (a store instalment card) isn't. The page states no minimum payment or interest-free period for ordinary purchases.
